### Observed differences

- In the later window, A22 appears in every trace (100%) instead of about 48% before; A27 and A28, each present in about 53% of traces before, no longer appear at all. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- The outgoing transition from A21 now goes to A22 in 100% of cases, whereas before it split among A22 (about 48%), A27 (about 27%) and A28 (about 26%). [DIR001]
- A22 now always follows A09 and A21, and always precedes A23; before, A22 followed A09/A21 in about 48% of cases and A23 appeared alone in about 53% of cases. [REL007, REL010, REL013]
- A07 now co-occurs with A22 in about 54% of traces (always before A22), up from about 25% before. [REL001]
- A08 occurs slightly later in the trace (mean position from about 0.065 to 0.082) and its gap to A09 shortens: the share of A08–A09 pairs one step apart rises from about 22% to about 42%. [POS001, LAG001]
- A21 and A23 are now always exactly two steps apart, whereas before about half were three steps apart. [LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process replaced a branch containing A27 and A28 with a single path through A22. In the later window, A27 and A28 are absent, A22 is executed in every case, and the routing from A21 goes exclusively to A22. This is directly and consistently shown by occurrence, direction, and relation indicators. The main competing explanation is sampling variation, but A27 and A28 were present in over half of the before traces, so their complete disappearance is unlikely to be a chance artifact. The evidence cannot show whether A27 and A28 were removed from the process definition or simply not executed in this window, but the change is large and coherent across multiple indicators.
